_about: 格斗's painted frames (tools/fighter-frames.py): each fighter's master (txt2img, or an edit of a `base` painting; the kept seed and words), the words naming who it is in every frame, each frame's pose sketch (lean, legF/legB/armF/armB as [upper, lower] degrees from straight down toward the facing side; `up` a lift, `rot` a fall, `width` room for a blade, `air`/`free` not stood on the ground, `fix` {dx, dy, s} placed by eye, `seed` the kept painting) and words, and the clips the board plays (fps, loop, `hit` the strike frame, `calm` the frames reduced motion keeps). 秦雁's master: txt2img seed 2; 沈小满's: an edit of his `base` (the v3 rig's painting, seed 2) toward his guard. 卢方 and 祁长松 (切磋 · 演武场, 2026-10-28): txt2img masters, seed 3 each; unarmed, their 33 frames on 秦雁's clips.

master.words: A tall young Chinese swordswoman of twenty, black hair gathered in a high bun with a wooden hairpin, a straight serious face, wearing a long pale blue-grey hanfu robe to the ankles with a white inner collar and wide sleeves, a dark blue-grey sash tied at the waist with its ends hanging, dark cloth shoes. She holds a plain straight Chinese jian sword with a brass guard in her right hand. She stands in a martial guard stance: knees slightly bent, weight low, the sword held out forward and level toward the right at chest height, the left hand raised open by her chest. Drawn in soft graphite pencil and light watercolour wash on warm aged paper, in the manner of an old Chinese book illustration, clean confident outlines, gentle shading. The whole figure from the top of the bun to the shoes, seen from the SIDE, facing RIGHT, alone on plain empty paper, no ground, no other objects, no text. Set in old rural China (Ming dynasty dress), not Japanese, not Western.

master.words: Repaint the same thin Chinese peasant boy from the first image — the same face, small top-knot of black hair with loose short hair, the same loose grey-brown patched hemp jacket tied with a rope belt, sleeves rolled to the forearm, the same baggy hemp trousers with frayed hems above the ankle, rope-bound straw sandals, EMPTY HANDS, no weapon, no bow, nothing on his back — in the pose of the second image: a martial-arts guard stance, knees bent, weight low and springy, both fists raised in front of his face and chest, chin tucked. Drawn in the same soft graphite pencil and light watercolour wash on warm aged paper as the first image, in the manner of an old Chinese book illustration, the whole figure from the top-knot to the sandals, seen from the side facing right, alone on plain empty paper, no ground, no other objects, no text. The second image is only a pose guide: copy its body pose exactly, never its grey shapes.

base.words: A thin Chinese peasant boy of fourteen with a small top-knot of black hair and loose short hair, wearing a plain loose grey-brown patched hemp jacket tied with a rope belt, sleeves rolled to the forearm, baggy hemp trousers ending above the ankle with frayed hems, rope-bound straw sandals. Seen exactly from the SIDE in full profile, the whole body from the top of the head to the feet, facing RIGHT. Standing in a wide stance like a paper shadow-puppet figure laid out for cutting: feet planted far apart, the front leg forward and the back leg behind with a clear gap of empty paper between the legs; the front arm held straight out forward and slightly down, away from the body, the back arm held straight out behind and slightly down, away from the body, both hands open, clear empty paper between each arm and the body. Calm face in profile.Drawn in soft graphite pencil and light watercolour wash on warm aged paper, in the manner of an old Chinese book illustration, clean confident outlines, gentle shading.  The subject ALONE in the middle of the picture with wide plain empty paper all around it, the paper even and clean, no ground, no shadow, no landscape, no other objects. Set in old rural China (Ming dynasty dress), not Japanese, not Western. Style: Chinese ink wash painting (shuimo with light colour) on warm aged sepia rice paper, loose xieyi brushwork, soft ink gradations from black to pale grey, the faintest muted mineral tint only where it carries meaning, in the manner of an old Chinese album leaf. No bright or saturated colour, no white paper, no pen hatching, no Western field-guide rendering, no photograph, no 3D. No text, no characters, no calligraphy, no seal, no signature, no border, no frame.
